newsitem.title: USA: Ohio voters defeat gambling issue.
newsitem.headline: Ohio voters defeat gambling issue.

text.p: Ohio voters firmly defeated a statewide measure that would have permitted riverboat gambling in four cities, state officials said Wednesday.
About 62 percent opposed the measure and 38 percent supported it in lighter-than-expected turnout, a spokeswoman for Ohio Secretary of State Bob Taft said.

Statewide Issue 1 would have permitted up to eight permanently moored riverboat casinos in Cleveland, Cincinnati, Youngstown and Lorain, with a percent of profits earmarked for the state's public schools.
Touted in heavy television advertising by a coalition that included several Ohio developers, the measure had the support of some large Ohio labor unions.
But Gov. George Voinovich led the fight against it, and most major Ohio newspapers opposed it in editorials.
Ohio has a state-run lottery and permits horserace betting and bingo.
Ohioans defeated a similar statewide casino proposal in 1990.
